rows.etymology: 131. Ku. indraiṇi ‘rainbow’ < OIA indradhanúṣ- ‘rainbow’ (1577) with many parallels in the northwest and in N. indreni; Turner asks whether the N. -r- is borrowed from OIA, but more plausible is the assumption of cluster preservation shared by the languages of the northwestern branch. Note also West Pahāṛī indru nāga ‘name of a snake god’ (Handa [2001: 58]) and borrowing into TB Kann. indrŏmöṅ ‘month September-October’ (≃ OIA āśvina-).
